item.title: Spectral correction factors for the removal of glint perturbations in above-water radiometry
item.description:
Spectral correction factors for the removal of glint perturbations in above-water radiometry
Barbara Bulgarelli, Davide D'Alimonte, Giuseppe Zibordi, and Tamito Kajiyama
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8971–8988, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8971-2026, 2026
Spectral glint correction factors for above-water radiometric measurements were computed for diverse atmospheric, wind and illumination conditions typical of inland, coastal and open-ocean waters, via deterministic and stochastic radiative transfer simulations. The observation geometry of the Ocean Color component of the Aerosol Robotic Network was adopted. Correction factors for both total and diffuse sky radiance are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20609990.

item.title: UzSolarHeat Weather: a long-term-adjusted representative year for solar energy at 170 nodes over Uzbekistan
item.description:
UzSolarHeat Weather: a long-term-adjusted representative year for solar energy at 170 nodes over Uzbekistan
Azizboy Khaitmukhamedov, Dilshod Jalilov, Murodbek Kuralov, Abdurauf Usmanov, and Oybek Abdulkhaev
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-896,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Solar plants in Uzbekistan are planned with typical-year weather files rarely checked against the ground. We release 510 such hourly years for 170 points, with code, and test them at 13 stations, partly with Soviet records digitised here. Total sunlight agrees, but direct sunlight is 13 % low. A ground-calibrated level, released alongside, corrects this and lowers the estimated cost of solar heat by 8 %. A month-selection bias we remove also appears at 651 points across Africa and Asia.

item.title: Global network of virtual coastal stations from altimetry-based sea level data
item.description:
Global network of virtual coastal stations from altimetry-based sea level data
Lancelot Leclercq, Anny Cazenave, Fabien Léger, Florence Birol, Marcello Passaro, Fernando Niño, Léna Tolu, Jean-François Legeais, Svetlana Jevrejeva, and Sarah Connors
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-934,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
The present data set, based on a dedicated reprocessing of the altimetry data from the Jason-1, 2, 3 and Sentinel-6A Michael Frielich missions provides 23-year-long time series of coastal sea level change at a network of 1653 virtual stations located very close to the coast. This dataset can be used to study the interannual variability and trends in sea level along the world coastlines. It completes the current tide gauge network.

item.title: A photographic, taxonomic and environmental dataset of fish eggs and larvae in the south-central Tyrrhenian Sea, 2021–2025
item.description:
A photographic, taxonomic and environmental dataset of fish eggs and larvae in the south-central Tyrrhenian Sea, 2021–2025
Gianluca Liguori, Ylenia Carotenuto, Giorgio Dall'Olmo, Antonia Chiarore, Alice Mirasole, Daniela Cianelli, and Lorenzo Ciannelli
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-952,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We share photographs and identifications of more than 2,300 fish larvae and 3,000 fish eggs collected between 2021 and 2025 in two underwater canyons and at a long-term coastal station near Naples, Italy, together with measurements of seawater properties. Each larva is linked to its photograph, so the dataset can help train taxonomists and computer programs that recognise fish larvae, and support studies on when and where fish reproduce in the Mediterranean Sea.

item.title: GLOBES: the Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States
item.description:
GLOBES: the Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States
Gabrielle Pereira Quadrado, Ivan David Haigh, Meghana Nagaraj, Ben Samuel Hague, José Eduardo Carneiro-Barros, Samuel T. Wilson, Philip R. Thompson, and Thomas Wahl
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-961,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Ocean wave observations help predict coastal hazards, guide surfing and navigation, inform infrastructure design, and support climate research. However, wave buoy data are scattered across many organizations and provided in different formats, making them hard to combine. We standardized 1,665 wave buoy records from 27 providers in 41 countries to make historical measurements easier to find, compare, and reuse. This public library supports scientific research, engineering, and coastal management.
